A.rule: a non-ledger_app session blocked ledger_app sessions in 52 samples; 298 pool acquisition timeouts

report.summary: After the 04:34:11 restart the pool was set to max 1 with a 250 ms timeout. An idle-in-transaction session blocked the one connection, causing pool timeouts and failed transfers (500/503). The link to the 500/503 responses is inferred.

findings.claim: A restart at 04:34:11 cut poolMaximumSize from 10 to 1 and connection timeout from 30000 ms to 250 ms.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows both values changing at the restart inside the window.

findings.claim: The 1-connection pool timed out on acquisition (298 timeouts) while pending borrowers and active connections appeared only from 04:34:18.
findings.reason: Pool metrics show configured max 1, 250 ms timeout, 298 acquisition timeouts, and pending/active above zero from 04:34:18.

findings.claim: A session idle in a transaction blocked another session from 04:34:18 to 04:36:16, which fits the pool starvation and transfer failures (38% server errors).
findings.reason: The blocking window matches the pool pressure and the 500/503 errors (50 and 172 of 580 requests); no direct request-to-timeout link was observed.

findings.claim: Outbox throughput fell sharply after the restart, while deliveries that did happen were fast and successful.
findings.reason: Arrivals dropped from about 38 to about 1-5 per 10 s bucket; all 379 deliveries succeeded in about 71 ms, so the consumer is not the problem.

limitations: One 10 s scrape gap, a counter restart, and NaN gauge samples limit the metrics, and the 2 s blocker sampling can miss short blocks.
No evidence shows which code path left the session idle in a transaction, or why the restart changed the pool settings.
